result.rationale: The new util `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `refreshTokenResponse` which is the result of `schema.safeParse(response)` — a `{success, data}` wrapper, not the parsed data. In googlecalendar CalendarService the diff stores that wrapper verbatim: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); ... data: { key }`, whereas the old line was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`. So the credential key becomes the wrapper object, breaking subsequent schema parses of the stored credential.

judged_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` returns the zod SafeParseReturn wrapper `{success, data}` and that wrapper is written verbatim as `credential.key`, so after the first successful refresh (sync enabled or not) every subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor throws and the user's Google Calendar integration is permanently broken.
